subject: Science
title: Forces, space and climate questions
objective_verbatim: Consolidate forces, space and climate; answer scientific questions.
reading_age_est: rough ARI grade 4.33 on 844 pupil-visible words; heuristic age guide 10.33 years, not a formal reading-age test
pupil_words: choose a model that fits a science question and use a matching clue.
success_criteria: I can match a question to a model.
I can give a claim with a matching clue.
I can say one thing the model cannot show.

vocab.definition: a push or pull on an object
vocab.example: Friction is a force that can slow a toy.
Earth’s rotation brings day and night.

vocab.definition: an observation or result that supports a claim
vocab.example: The shorter run is evidence for my answer.
A hot day alone does not show a climate trend.

retrieval.question: Give one link in the warming chain.
retrieval.answer: Burning fossil fuel adds carbon dioxide; extra greenhouse gas slows heat loss.

retrieval.question: Name one fact our Solar System cards support.
retrieval.answer: The Sun is a star; Earth orbits it; or the Moon orbits Earth.

retrieval.question: How can friction affect a moving toy?

stages.pupil_text: Match each question to a kit card: toy and surface, globe and torch, or warming chain.
stages.adult_text: Offer a predictable seat or standing spot and the first visual cue. No public test.

stages.pupil_text: Think back. Say, point or write one answer for each question.
stages.adult_text: Ask three low-stakes retrieval questions; prior coverage must be checked.

stages.pupil_text: I choose a toy for a motion question. The toy went less far on rough paper in this run. I must repeat before I claim why.
stages.adult_text: Model the full reasoning step, pre-teach four words and ask the show-me question.

stages.pupil_text: Torch and ball are chosen for day and night. Add the missing clue. Say why it fits.
stages.adult_text: Show the part-done example, then allow paired talk before an answer. One-minute reset inside this stage.

stages.pupil_text: A toy travels less far on rough paper in this example. Choose the best idea to test.
stages.adult_text: All pupils answer the four-option hinge; use the decision rule, not a score.

stages.pupil_text: Choose two stations. Give a claim and matching clue for each. Name one limit.
stages.adult_text: One adult supports agreed pupils, the other holds the group; swap across the week. One-minute reset inside this stage.

stages.pupil_text: Does your clue fit? Fix one clue or add a limit.
stages.adult_text: Give a specific verbal comment (VF) and invite one self-edit (//) or read-back (?).

stages.pupil_text: Name a model, claim and clue. Say what changed after feedback.
stages.adult_text: Hear the answer and name how it changes the next example or support. One-minute reset and handoff.

worked_example.full: Toy motion question → choose toy and surface → measure distance → test friction as one cause.
worked_example.faded: Day and night question → choose torch and ball → observe ____ → explain Earth’s turn.
worked_example.removed_step: Name the observation of the marked place moving away from the light.
worked_example.fade_next: Next time omit the model choice, so the pupil chooses a suitable model before looking for a clue.

cfu.question: If my question is about day and night, should I point to the toy or torch-and-ball?

hinge.question: A model trolley stops sooner on a mat than on a smooth board. Which idea is relevant to test?

options.diagnosis: Transfers a space model to a surface-and-motion question.
Uses daylight rather than the changed surface to explain the trolley run.

options.text: The climate of the whole Earth.
options.diagnosis: Uses a whole-Earth climate pattern for a local trolley test.

hinge.decision_rule: About 3 in 4 or more right → move on. Otherwise re-model with the named I-do example, then ask the parallel hinge.
hinge.parallel_hinge: A block is pulled over two surfaces. Which idea helps test why the pull differs: friction or Earth’s rotation? Answer: friction.

misconceptions.misconception: Any science model can answer any question.
misconceptions.spot: Pupil chooses A, a space model for trolley motion.
misconceptions.correction: Match the model’s observable feature to the question before making a claim.

misconceptions.misconception: One different toy run proves roughness alone caused it.
misconceptions.spot: Pupil chooses B correctly but then claims one run proves the cause without controls.
misconceptions.correction: Repeat runs with a consistent start and push before treating the difference as strong evidence.

we_do.support: Show the torch and marked ball; point to the place that moves into shade.
we_do.stretch: Explain why a toy run cannot test a climate claim even when it gives a clear result.
we_do.F: Show the torch and marked ball; point to the place that moves into shade.
we_do.M: Give an answer and a matching clue.
we_do.H: Explain why a toy run cannot test a climate claim even when it gives a clear result.

tiers.F: Match a question to a model.
tiers.M: Give an answer and a matching clue.
tiers.H: Compare two models, clues and limits.

stems.M: My claim is ___; the clue is ___.
stems.H: The ___ model fits because ___, but it cannot show ___.

tiers.go_deeper: Compare two models: what can each show and miss?
tiers.early_finisher: Two toy runs differ on one surface. Can friction alone explain this? Choose one control that would help.

adaptations.cognition_learning: Use three labelled kit photos matched to three question cards, then remove labels.
adaptations.communication_interaction: Let a partner rehearse claim and clue with the M/H frame before recording.
adaptations.semh: Offer a known station role and a quiet check-in before changing stations.
adaptations.sensory_physical: Keep kits on a fixed tray and allow a staff-captured photo of a real demonstration.
adaptations.eal: Pre-teach force, rotation and climate with icons; allow home-language planning and M/H explanation frames.

speaking_frames: My claim is ___; the clue is ___.
The ___ model fits because ___, but it cannot show ___.

ta_focus.i_do: Listen: first I read the question, then choose the matching kit.
ta_focus.we_do: Which model is already chosen? What observation is missing?
ta_focus.independent: Show me your claim; which clue did you find on your own?

prompt_ladder: Point to the lesson’s diagram, kit or source.
Ask: What is done, and what is the next step?
Model one step, then return the next step to the pupil.
Finish one example together, then fade the help.

F.q: Which kit is for a motion question?
Which kit is for day and night?

M.q: Why do we name a clue?
Why is one toy run weak evidence?
M.a: The start or push might have changed.

H.q: What can the torch-and-ball model not show exactly?
H.a: True size and distance, among other details.

H.q: Why does a warming card not show a local force?
H.a: It represents a long-term causal chain, not the toy’s motion.

items: Day and night → torch and ball
interactions.answer_key: Match as listed; buttons give live feedback.

items: One toy run proves the surface caused a difference
A torch-and-ball model can show day and night
interactions.answer_key: First false; repeat with controls. Second true as a simplified model.

diagrams.alt: Three panels show a toy on rough and smooth surfaces, a torch shining on a turning ball, and a schematic long climate line beside one isolated weather day. The line is not measured data.
diagrams.caption: Choose a model: toy and surface, torch and ball, or long climate record. Sketches are simplified; the climate line is not data.

practical.prediction: Which surface may let the same toy travel farther?
method: Mark one start and use the same toy.
Launch twice on each surface in the same way.
Measure each run and record it.
Use other models only for their own questions.
practical.risk: Check against the school risk assessment and CLEAPSS guidance. Keep kit at desk height and torch light out of eyes. Do not infer a cause from one uncontrolled run.
practical.pupil_risk: A moving toy may hit someone or fall from the table.
practical.pupil_safety: Use a low clear track. Keep hands and faces away from the run.

facts.claim: Force is a push or pull; friction is a contact force.
A toy’s movement can be changed by contact forces, but one run cannot isolate a cause.

stages: Arrival (5 min): Match each question to a kit card: toy and surface, globe and torch, or warming chain. Staff: Offer a predictable seat or standing spot and the first visual cue. No public test.
Starter (3 min): Think back. Say, point or write one answer for each question. Staff: Ask three low-stakes retrieval questions; prior coverage must be checked.

I Do (5 min): I choose a toy for a motion question. The toy went less far on rough paper in this run. I must repeat before I claim why. Staff: Model the full reasoning step, pre-teach four words and ask the show-me question.

We Do (7 min): Torch and ball are chosen for day and night. Add the missing clue. Say why it fits. Staff: Show the part-done example, then allow paired talk before an answer. One-minute reset inside this stage.
We Do 2 (5 min): A toy travels less far on rough paper in this example. Choose the best idea to test. Staff: All pupils answer the four-option hinge; use the decision rule, not a score.

Independent (8 min): Choose two stations. Give a claim and matching clue for each. Name one limit. Staff: One adult supports agreed pupils, the other holds the group; swap across the week. One-minute reset inside this stage.
Review (4 min): Does your clue fit? Fix one clue or add a limit. Staff: Give a specific verbal comment (VF) and invite one self-edit (//) or read-back (?).
Exit (3 min): Name a model, claim and clue. Say what changed after feedback. Staff: Hear the answer and name how it changes the next example or support. One-minute reset and handoff.

if_behind.must_teach_core: Choose two stations. Give a claim and matching clue for each. Name one limit. Preserve the individual evidence required above.
if_behind.shorten_or_merge: After a secure hinge, shorten repeated oral rehearsal. If needed, merge the exit reflection into the Arrival of Autumn 2 W06. Keep the core evidence and any safety teaching; record the change and coverage impact.
if_behind.next_lesson: Autumn 2 W06: Consolidate and revisit key ideas through investigation.
if_behind.dependency: Pass on today’s checked understanding and unresolved hinge errors for the next starter. Do not replace incomplete individual work with a group product.

target_links.Cognition & learning: We do: Name the observation of the marked place moving away from the light. Record the pupil’s own sequencing, attention or independence target, including the prompt level needed.
target_links.Communication & interaction: Check: respond to “A model trolley stops sooner on a mat than on a smooth board. Which idea is relevant to test?” in the pupil’s agreed mode. Evidence an individual communication/turn-taking target without requiring speech.
target_links.SEMH: Arrival: Match each question to a kit card: toy and surface, globe and torch, or warming chain. Use the agreed predictable start or pause/re-entry plan; evidence the pupil’s own regulation or engagement target privately.
target_links.Sensory/physical: Independent: Choose two stations. Give a claim and matching clue for each. Name one limit. Offer the agreed accessible input, enlarged material or adapted equipment; record the pupil’s target-related access/independence, not a diagnosis.
target_links.EAL: Model/shared rehearsal: use force, rotation, evidence, climate with the actual example; allow first-language planning and oral rehearsal before the independent response. Record the agreed language target; EAL is not SEN.

planning_entry.target_recording: Capture E against the pupil's own IEDP target on the school's evidence app; the IEDP carries their EHCP-linked and Boxall targets, so one record serves every plan. Follow the pupil's IBSP where it differs from these routines.
